races.name: West 'Howya' Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Whats New
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with four career top-three finishes on similar Good ground, and Andrew Slattery's 3/32 trainer strike rate is modest but Cian Quirke keeps horses handy; the 9-day turnaround is short but manageable for a 4-year-old with a light weight history.

runners_data.name: Alfinthesea
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and style genuinely unknown, so tactical position on the day is unpredictable; Kieren Buckley and Edward Buckley (trainer) is a tight combination but the absence of recent form history makes this a significant unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Breezingwithdstars
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator who has repeatedly faded in the finish — their 0W0P record in four runs on similar Going is a concern, and the hg:p (pacifier/hood) suggests a tendency to idle or hang rather than battle; J J Slevin's class is the main positive in an otherwise uninspiring profile.

runners_data.name: First Ascent
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy and Gordon Elliott is a powerful combination that demands respect, and First Ascent has shown placed form in similar-distance, Good-ground novice company; the 70-day absence is notable and they race from hold-up, needing a strong pace to produce their run.

runners_data.name: Kilmond Knight
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just one run on record (a pulled-up over 22f) and no trainer recent strike rate, making form assessment nearly impossible; Alan O'Sullivan claims 5lb but this horse's jumping and stamina are entirely untested in this field.

runners_data.name: Minnatrix
runners_data.note: Prominent to hold-up profile (hg:h — hood) with a solid second on similar Good ground among their form figures, and Eoin McCarthy's 1/15 T14 is low but the horse appears consistent enough to stay in contention; G B Noonan should be able to place them handily behind the leader.

runners_data.name: No Mon No Fun
runners_data.note: Fell last time and pulled up before that, giving this a fragile jumping profile entering a 13-runner maiden hurdle; Philip Donovan and Jack Doyle have no recent stable form (0/0 T14), and the horse's hold-up tendency means it needs to jump cleanly throughout to be a factor.

runners_data.name: Rumi Rock
runners_data.note: Has faded badly in the finish across multiple runs and their sole similar-Going run produced a 10th, so the finishing profile here is weak; Phillip Enright's experience helps but the 55-day break and a pattern of weakening late does not suit a race that could become a sprint from the last.

runners_data.name: Sharu
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe for Henry De Bromhead is a strong rider-trainer pairing, and a second place in their most recent Good-ground run over 16f shows Sharu can be competitive when the conditions suit; prominent style and a lower OR of 98 means they get into this on favourable terms relative to the 120s.

runners_data.name: World As One
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, giving them an automatic lead, and the Mullins yard rarely runs them without purpose; however, their last three runs (5th, 4th, 5th) after showing ability when second suggests they are capable but vulnerable when challenged at the business end.

runners_data.name: Lady Felicia
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just one run (4th over 16f on Good), and the 56-day break plus genuinely unknown style make her an opaque proposition; Simon Torrens is an experienced handler and the hg:t (tongue-tie) is a small positive, but 151lbs and a single run is thin evidence.

runners_data.name: Middlethird Marvel
runners_data.note: A persistent fader with five consecutive runs without a top-six finish, and their hg:tp (tongue-tie and pacifier) combination alongside Conor Smithers' 7lb claim is not enough to offset a deeply uninspiring record; hold-up style with a fading pattern at this trip on Good is a difficult profile to back.

runners_data.name: Phyllis Rodda
runners_data.note: A 275-day absence is a major flag — this is effectively an unknown quantity returning from a near-nine-month break with a PP- form string and no recent going data; Mark Walsh's jockeyship is top-class but Barry Connell's 0/1 T14 and the lengthy absence make this a speculative interest at best.

races.paceDynamic: World As One (Mullins/Sean O'Keeffe) is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-horse maiden hurdle over 2m1½f on Good ground at Ballinrobe, and with no other horse mapped to lead, they can set a wholly uncontested, controlled gallop from the front. Whats New, Minnatrix, and Sharu are the prominent types who will likely track close behind, meaning the early pace is unlikely to be pressured but also unlikely to be dawdling given the size of the field. World As One's recent form shows a tendency to fade (finishing 2nd, 4th, 5th), suggesting they can get first run but may not sustain it to the line, which opens the door for prominent trackers to pounce. This race shape — a single, relaxed pace-setter setting a sustainable tempo — most favours horses racing prominently just off the leader, as they can save ground, avoid trouble, and strike before hold-up horses can finish their runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If World As One bowls along at a comfortable tempo and a prominent tracker times their move from the second fence out.
scenarios.body: World As One sets an uncontested pace on the inside, but their tendency to weaken late means a close-following prominent runner can collar them approaching the last hurdle; the Good ground rewards horses travelling smoothly throughout rather than making one late surge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If World As One finds more than their form suggests and the pace is genuinely pedestrian, killing the finish for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A truly slow-run race would allow World As One to control and quicken on their own terms, leaving midfielders and hold-up horses with insufficient time to close; the Mullins/O'Keeffe combination at a provincial maiden is not to be underestimated tactically.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Runners Swamp Them
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is just fast enough to stretch the field and hold-up horses get a clean passage from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A moderate-but-honest gallop with 13 runners can create a concertina effect turning for home, and hold-up horses such as First Ascent (Jack Kennedy, Gordon Elliott) and Breezingwithdstars could benefit if traffic opens up; however, both have form concerns with fading and both need everything to fall right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Fallers Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes interference, fallers, or a bunching of hold-up horses that leaves the race to a survivor.
scenarios.body: With 13 runners, several lightly-raced or inconsistent types (Kilmond Knight, No Mon No Fun, Phyllis Rodda), and a maiden-hurdle context, incidents over the obstacles are plausible and could promote a well-placed prominent type by default.

watchPoints.text: World As One leads uncontested but has finished 4th and 5th in their last two runs — watch for them to weaken from the second-last hurdle, which is the key moment that will determine whether a prominent or hold-up horse wins.

Phyllis Rodda returns from 275 days off for Mark Walsh — an elite jockey booking on a lightly raced mare after such a gap could signal market support; watch the SP as a significant drift or shortening will carry information.

With 13 runners in a maiden hurdle on a right-handed track at Ballinrobe, the field will bunch at the initial hurdles — Kilmond Knight (previous unfinished run) and No Mon No Fun (fell last time) are both jumping liabilities to monitor early.

Sharu's OR of 98 versus a field of 120-rated rivals looks advantageous on paper, but Henry De Bromhead's horses have been in moderate form (5/30 T14) — watch whether Darragh O'Keeffe settles them prominently or drops in, as position will define their chance.

First Ascent is Jack Kennedy's sole ride in this race and Elliott's T14 is 9/48 — in a maiden hurdle at this level, Kennedy will look to improve their position from hold-up after the third-last; if traffic clears on the home turn, they become the primary danger to the prominent runners.

races.name: David Heneghan Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bhean Saibhre
runners_data.note: Clear front-runner who should face no pace pressure here; Peter Smithers (7) claim softens the weight burden, Howard yard without a win in 14-day window, but the horse's biggest asset is the uncontested lead — the STYLE_FIT tag is a mild caution given she is officially rated prominent rather than lead, but the race shape is entirely in her favour.

runners_data.name: Houndsworth
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with genuine Good-ground winning form at 16f and a respectable 1W1P from four similar-going runs; Phillip Enright is a solid booking, the 37-day absence is manageable, and if the pace scenario opens up late he is the one most capable of a sustained finish.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer with an excellent 11/11 strike-rate on Good going; J J Slevin is a high-profile booking for Ryan's yard who are 5/25 in the 14-day window, and Le Diablo's 2/17f form on this ground makes him the most natural challenger to the leader.

runners_data.name: Doctor Confusion
runners_data.note: A huge unknown after 349 days off the track; De Bromhead's yard is operating at 5/30 over 14 days, the horse's style is unclassified, and his last four runs on similar ground show no wins or places — this is very much a resurrection gamble.

runners_data.name: Valsorpresa
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up specialist with an excellent 15/15 Good-ground entries in similar conditions, recording 1W3P; Harry Sexton (7) is an inexperienced claimer and the 56-day break is modest, but this horse's consistency on this going profile makes it the most reliable of the hold-up group.

runners_data.name: Marlpark
runners_data.note: Ryan's second runner; a natural hold-up operator who sits deeper than his shown midfield position suggests — he has been redistributed forward on the map purely due to the volume of hold-up horses, and his actual race will be run from further back. His best form came on Soft going and his Good-ground record (9/15) is less compelling.

runners_data.name: Max Meridius
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in finishes, which is a critical negative in a slowly-run race where the field will likely sprint from the last; Mullins family booking is noted but Good-ground strike-rate of 5/13 without a win across 16f+ races makes this profile hard to back.

runners_data.name: Ballinvasas Best
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who is a genuine hold-up type shifted forward on the pace map to midfield because the rear is overcrowded with closers; his form shows four runs on Good going all finishing 4th or worse, and there is no win in his recent history — a horse carrying the minimum weight but with limited scope.

runners_data.name: At The Wings
runners_data.note: Kenneally (5) claim reduces the weight, but this six-year-old's last five runs on Good ground include no wins or places and a 7/20f effort nine days ago — the short turnaround and the redistribution away from his natural hold-up role both weigh against him in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Bhean Saibhre is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should dictate a controlled, measured gallop over this 2m1½f trip on Good ground at Ballinrobe. Le Diablo is the only other natural prominent racer and will track Bhean Saibhre, but without a rival pressing the leader the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching — a single-figure field at this pace almost certainly produces a steady-to-moderate gallop with a proper test reserved for the home straight. The hold-up battalion — Houndsworth, Valsorpresa, Max Meridius, Marlpark, Ballinvasas Best, and At The Wings — all want to come from off the pace, but the field holds more hold-up horses than can all find clear daylight late; Marlpark, Ballinvasas Best, and At The Wings have been redistributed to midfield as they are unlikely to sit as deep as their true style demands. This race shape — an uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable pace with no pressure — heavily favours prominent racers and horses who can travel close to the pace and pounce in the straight, rather than those who need a genuine test of stamina to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bhean Saibhre Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Bhean Saibhre dictates an uncontested, confidence-boosting gallop and the hold-up cavalry cannot close enough.
scenarios.body: Bhean Saibhre leads in her own time, the moderate tempo preserves her stamina reserves, and the field simply cannot summon the sustained finishing speed to bridge the gap on Good ground; Le Diablo is best placed to challenge tracking just off the pace but may lack the sharp turn of foot to reel in a horse loose in front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop steadies sufficiently that Le Diablo or a stalker can quicken past a tiring Bhean Saibhre in the final flight.
scenarios.body: Le Diablo has winning form at 17f on Good ground and travels prominently; if Bhean Saibhre ties up slightly after the last, a horse with a clean jump and a gear can collar her.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Break
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected — perhaps Le Diablo pushes Bhean Saibhre wide or makes errors — and the closer group benefits from a genuine test.
scenarios.body: Houndsworth landed a handicap hurdle at 16f on Good and Valsorpresa has a solid record at this course distance on this ground; a genuine stamina test would play to their profiles if they can find a run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Outsider Delivers Upset
scenarios.trigger: If chaos or jumping errors disrupt the front two and a midfield horse quickens through the gaps late.
scenarios.body: Doctor Confusion returns from a lengthy 349-day absence for De Bromhead but the layoff is a serious unknown; Max Meridius fades in finishes and At The Wings has a deeply modest form profile.

watchPoints.text: Bhean Saibhre's jumping — if she makes a significant error at any flight she loses her uncontested lead advantage immediately, fundamentally reshaping this race for Le Diablo and the hold-up group.

Le Diablo's jumping fluency matters critically here; J J Slevin will want to track the leader without losing contact, and any clumsy hurdle could strand him in no-man's-land between the front-runner and the closers.

The redistribution of Marlpark, Ballinvasas Best, and At The Wings means the genuine hold-up group is larger than the map shows — if the pace is moderate, multiple horses will be queuing for the same narrow late run and traffic problems are a real risk from the second-last onward.

Houndsworth's form record (8017-6) includes a prominent 0 and 1 on Good ground at 16f; if he travels sweetly for Phillip Enright and gets first run on the closers turning in, he becomes the biggest danger to the front-running scenario.
Doctor Confusion's 349-day absence under De Bromhead is worth monitoring in the paddock — well-being signs could upgrade or downgrade the significance of his unclassified style and form completely.

races.name: RBC Brewin Dolphin Rated Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Lureka Du Noyer
runners_data.note: Won most recent on Good ground (1/16f/GOO) and has 54 days between runs; De Bromhead sends this confirmed pace-setter to Ballinrobe with solid fitness evidence, though its STYLE_FIT flag reflects that its prominence role becomes slightly out of character — its best chance is controlling from the front unchallenged.

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: Elliott's runner has winning form on Good (1/20f/GOO) and arrives fresh at 17 days; by nature a prominent racer, but this field's pace density means the horse may not secure the position it wants — the redistribution to midfield reflects that tactical squeeze, not any loss of ability.

runners_data.name: Manoir De Mirande
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy partners a four-year-old who won last time on Good over 18f and has placed five times in nine Good-ground starts; naturally prominent and correctly mapped, this horse is the one that fits this race shape without any redistribution caveat and profiles as the chief beneficiary of Lureka's honest gallop.

runners_data.name: Crystabel
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's mare won last time on Good (1/18f/GOO) and boasts eight placings from nine Good-ground efforts, demonstrating strong going suitability; though a natural front-runner by inclination, the crowded prominent tier means she is likely to be covered up against her instincts, which tempers her chance in this shape.

runners_data.name: Eyeeye
runners_data.note: Carries a fades-in-finish warning and has managed just three placings from 15 Good-ground runs with no wins; a hold-up type by style, Paul John Gilligan's runner needs a strong pace to be set and clean jumping, but its finishing record makes it hard to trust as a finisher regardless of shape.

runners_data.name: Move It On Over
runners_data.note: Slevin partners an OR-74 runner with no wins or places from eight Good-ground outings and a fades-in-finish flag; the horse profiles as the most exposed and least threatening in the field and would require a wholesale collapse of the leaders to feature.

races.paceDynamic: Lureka Du Noyer is the confirmed front runner and, as the only true pace-setter in a six-runner field, will dictate from the front at a measured, uncontested gallop on Good ground at Ballinrobe. Manoir De Bromhead is the one prominent type able to slot in naturally behind, while Ardeen Joy and Crystabel — both genuine prominent racers by inclination — are pushed back in the mapping because there is more pace-hunting intent in this field than the front positions can physically accommodate; in practice one or both will be shuffled wider or slightly further back than ideal. Eyeeye and Move It On Over are genuine hold-up types but both carry a fade warning, limiting their ability to capitalise on any late collapse. The race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who can track Lureka Du Noyer at close range and pounce before the hold-up horses can get involved — Manoir De Mirande, the one properly-placed prominent type in the map, is the profile this shape most naturally rewards.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lureka Sets, Manoir Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Lureka Du Noyer leads at a comfortable clip and Manoir De Mirande tracks in second throughout.
scenarios.body: Lureka Du Noyer controls tempo without pressure, keeping the race honest but not punishing, and Manoir De Mirande's recent winning form on Good ground (1/18f/GOO) puts him in the perfect position to pounce from the last hurdle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Ardeen Joy or Crystabel forces their natural position near the front, creating genuine competition for early prominence.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace raises the tempo and stretches the field, making Lureka Du Noyer work harder to maintain the lead than in the uncontested scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Lureka Du Noyer goes unchallenged and increases the tempo from the front, using its front-running fitness to grind out a wire-to-wire success.
scenarios.body: With no serious challenger pressing and hold-up types carrying fade warnings, Lureka Du Noyer could simply be too far clear turning in for rivals to reel in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a late run for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Eyeeye and Move It On Over would need a fast-run race and clean jumping to finish, but both carry explicit fade warnings and neither has the form to suggest they can sustain a meaningful challenge.

watchPoints.text: Manoir De Mirande — if Jack Kennedy is able to slot directly onto Lureka Du Noyer's quarters from the outset, this horse has the correct profile, recent winning form, and going credentials to be the primary danger throughout.

Ardeen Joy and Crystabel — watch the first two hurdles closely to see whether either can force their way into the prominent position they want; if one succeeds, the race tempo changes and Scenario B becomes live.
Lureka Du Noyer's jumping — as the sole pace-setter, any hurdle error early on could allow Ardeen Joy or Crystabel to surge forward and disrupt the planned controlled gallop.

Eyeeye and Move It On Over — both carry fade warnings; if either is still in contention at the second-last, it may signal the pace has been slower than expected, which would reframe the entire race shape.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Wolf Prince
runners_data.note: Won twice at this trip on Good and enters freshly nine days after a win; genuine hold-up horse who needs something to chase and is best served if the pace picks up in the straight — headgear (p) suggests he needs the race run on his terms.

runners_data.name: Fiveonefive
runners_data.note: Mark Walsh takes the ride but a 23-day break and a string of disappointing finishes since a April win make it hard to trust him; natural hold-up type at a 168lb weight who has struggled when the pace has been steady in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Sir Allen
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner whose entire chance hinges on uncontested front position; the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects that anything pressuring him early would undermine his chance significantly, but with no rival for the lead he should get an easy time of it.

runners_data.name: Spinola Bay
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy partners a horse with a sharp recent form profile — two wins from 16f on Good and Soft — and if he follows up from prominent, he looks the most naturally placed to exploit a moderate pace; headgear (p) retained and trainer Elliott in form at 9/48 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Dontgowithjoe
runners_data.note: Long layoff of 328 days is the obvious concern, but won two in a row on Good before the break and if tuned up Simon Torrens has a horse with pace at the weights — needs the race to really develop late to maximise his finish.

runners_data.name: Ballyearl
runners_data.note: De Bromhead runner arrives 21 days after a run in hood (t), has shown ability over Good ground with a win from 17f, but also has a couple of weak recent performances — Darragh O'Keeffe could push from prominent and be ideally placed if he finds his form again.

runners_data.name: Eye Of A Tiger
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin aboard a horse whose natural tendency is to race from the rear, but the crowded hold-up sector means he has been pushed into the map's midfield — at a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 racing out of role is a genuine risk, and his recent form (5U69) does not inspire confidence at 147lbs.

runners_data.name: Eye Contact
runners_data.note: The fades-in-finish flag is damaging in a race likely to require a strong late effort; naturally a hold-up type forced into a midfield mapping by field composition, and a trainer strike rate of 0/1 over 14 days alongside consistent poor finishes (00-46) makes this hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Free Flow
runners_data.note: Off 121 days and a hold-up performer by nature, Free Flow has been slotted into the midfield map only because the field is saturated with rear-of-field horses — the STYLE_FIT compromise, combined with recent form showing five double-figure finishes, is a significant red flag.

runners_data.name: Space Warrior
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins runner returns after 98 days and has flashes of ability — a third from 17f on Good being the standout — but like the other redistributed runners sits in a compromised map position and has not won at this distance; Cian Quirke on a horse that needs a strong pace to deliver its finish.

races.paceDynamic: Sir Allen is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, should be allowed to dictate from the front at a comfortable, self-selected tempo on Good ground at Ballinrobe. That controlled, sustainable gallop means the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, creating a race that will be run at a steady-to-moderate rhythm before quickening in the home straight — a shape that typically rewards horses travelling well in behind rather than those grinding from the back. The field is unusually hold-up heavy, with Wolf Prince, Fiveonefive, Dontgowithjoe and Space Warrior all genuine off-the-pace types, yet Eye Of A Tiger, Eye Contact and Free Flow — also natural hold-up horses — have been redistributed to the map's midfield positions because there are simply too many rear-of-field types to accommodate; of those, Spinola Bay and Ballyearl are best placed to secure prominent positions directly behind Sir Allen. The tactical verdict is clear: a one-dimensional front-runner setting a genteel gallop on Good ground favours well-handicapped prominent-to-midfield horses who can travel handy and pounce early in the straight, with true hold-up horses relying on a late sprint that the moderate tempo may not generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sir Allen Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Allen is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a fair but unhurried pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Sir Allen dictates on his own terms and the race becomes a procession until the final two hurdles, where horses travelling prominently — Spinola Bay and Ballyearl — have the prime position to pounce without needing to make up ground. Closers are left with too little fuel in the tank to bridge the gap on a flat track with a steady tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Get The Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens markedly from halfway, stringing the field out and creating genuine ground for late closers.
scenarios.body: A stronger mid-race surge — perhaps triggered by Ballyearl or Spinola Bay moving early — could burn off Sir Allen and open a clear lane for Wolf Prince and Dontgowithjoe to finish with purpose. Both have course-relevant Good-ground form and Wolf Prince in particular arrives fresh off a nine-day turnaround having won over this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sir Allen Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate that Sir Allen simply idles into the straight and kicks clear before rivals can organise a challenge.
scenarios.body: On a flat, galloping track like Ballinrobe, a front-runner who has stolen a march in the final half-mile can prove very hard to reel in when the hold-up brigade has left themselves too much to do. Sir Allen has a win from 14f on Heavy suggesting he can produce a finish, and a lone break at the right moment would expose the lack of pace in the chasing pack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If early scrimmaging for prominent positions between Spinola Bay, Ballyearl and the redistributed midfield horses pushes the early tempo beyond Sir Allen's comfort zone.
scenarios.body: A quicker-than-expected clip would suit the genuine stay-back types who bide their time, but this depends on horses tagged as redistributed — Eye Of A Tiger, Free Flow and Eye Contact — racing out of their true role, which is structurally unlikely given the field shape. Even in this scenario the beneficiaries would more likely be Wolf Prince or Dontgowithjoe than the style-compromised redistributed runners.

watchPoints.text: Wolf Prince and Dontgowithjoe are the two genuine hold-up horses with the strongest form credentials; if the pace does pick up from the back of the second-last, watch for both to quicken through tired horses — any late market move on Wolf Prince should be respected given his freshness.

Sir Allen's chance is entirely binary — if anything moves to challenge him for the lead before halfway, his STYLE_FIT flag suggests his chance collapses almost immediately; watch the early exchanges to see whether Spinola Bay or Ballyearl make an aggressive move for second position that could unsettle his rhythm.

Eye Contact carries a fades-in-finish flag on a course where hold-up horses are already compromised by the map — a moderate pace on Good ground makes it very unlikely she can sustain a challenge when asked for her effort, and layers should note the flag before taking a position.

The volume of redistributed runners (Eye Of A Tiger, Eye Contact, Free Flow, Space Warrior) means the map's midfield could become congested entering the straight; watch for traffic issues around the third-last as these horses jockey for gaps they are not naturally drawn to occupy.

Ballinrobe's Good going has remained consistent through all eight races on the card — pace figures are reliable and there is no ground-degradation concern to alter the tactical read as the card progresses toward the 6:39.

races.name: Sweeney Oil Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Tannery Park
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who fades late (flagged), returning after 420 days off — Mark Walsh in the saddle is the key angle, and sim-going form is positive (1W2P in 8 runs), but the long absence and finishing pattern are concerns at 2m6f.|

runners_data.name: Bearami Creek
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with solid Good-ground credentials (1W2P in 13 sim-going runs) who hasn't run in 72 days; no fade flag which distinguishes him from several rivals, but a big field suits his patient style only if the pace is genuinely strong.|

runners_data.name: Madame Masque
runners_data.note: Has a fade warning and returns after 205 days off; Darragh O'Keeffe takes over for De Bromhead but three recent runs at Dundalk on Heavier ground offer almost no guide to this Good-ground 2m6f hurdle.|

runners_data.name: It's Time Again
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who loves Good ground (1W4P in 15 runs) and has winning form at 22f — at 10 years old he is experienced enough to find a good position in a large field, and Liam McKenna's 3lb claim is a useful weight concession.|

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner; his style-fit score (0.93) flags he is racing somewhat out of role here, but in practice he is the only horse likely to lead and will control fractions — Good ground suits and he has winning form over similar trips.|

runners_data.name: Vroomvroomboo
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a solid 2m3f–2m7f record at Good; Conor Smithers' 7lb claim helps offset a modest OR of 86, but the horse's sim-going record (0W3P in 15) suggests he places rather than wins and a big field makes his task harder.|

runners_data.name: Coppola
runners_data.note: A horse with a string of placed efforts (three seconds, two pulls-up in last five) who is flagged for finishing fade; Joshua Halford's 7lb claim is notable for Gordon Elliott, and Good ground suits, but his consistent near-miss profile at 24f means he needs things to fall perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Ranger Billy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with two wins and three places from 15 Good-ground runs, handled well by J J Slevin — headgear (p) suggests he needs restraining, and the 2m6f trip over 10 hurdles is within his range based on previous form.|

runners_data.name: Whatyouwant
runners_data.note: Prominent type (headgear p) with two wins and two places on Good ground in 15 runs; ran only 11 days ago which suggests fitness, and his 2m5f–2m6f wins show the trip is tailor-made — G B Noonan knows this horse well.|

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: Bred and raced as a genuine hold-up horse but with five consecutive non-finishes or last-place efforts recently, he is also mapped to midfield because the field is stacked with closers; no wins or places on Good ground in 8 runs is deeply concerning.|

runners_data.name: Tantrum Boy
runners_data.note: A horse who naturally wants to be held up but finds himself mapped further forward than ideal in this shape; his best effort on Good ground was a third, but the overall record (0W0P in five Good runs) and a string of mid-pack finishes limit appeal.|

runners_data.name: Coole Vision
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer pushed into a midfield map by the weight of similar types — only one Good-ground run in nine attempts of any merit, and at OR 77 with a reserve jockey, this nine-year-old faces a stiff task even if the shape turns his way.|

runners_data.name: Will It Be You
runners_data.note: Fade-flagged hold-up horse (headgear p) whose Good-ground record across 15 runs (1W2P) looks decent in isolation, but finishing positions of 9, pulled-up, and 8 in recent starts tell a more worrying story; Brian Hayes brings experience but the trend is downward.|

runners_data.name: Lost Features
runners_data.note: Flagged for finishing fade and has been running every 9 days — freshness is not the issue but form (P,9,8,9,9 in recent starts) firmly is; a six-year-old who has not finished in the first half of the field in recent memory.|

runners_data.name: John Dixen
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type who is lightly framed for this competitive handicap; only one run in five that finished in a worthwhile position on Good ground, and Simon Torrens has a big field to navigate — the form is simply not there yet.|

runners_data.name: Sineads Fancy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer (headgear p) with a placed effort at 3 from this trip/going combination; 1W3P from 15 Good-ground runs is an honest record, and Cian Quirke's booking for a lightly-regarded yard is the most interesting angle here.|

runners_data.name: Light Her Up
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse placed into midfield on the race map because of the volume of closers — the 220-day layoff is significant, and the sim-going record (0W1P from 8) alongside a reserve jockey booking suggests connections are simply hoping for a run.|

runners_data.name: My Good Pal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer (headgear tp) with a career-best placed effort at 24f on Good, returned just 18 days ago — Gavin Cromwell's strong record with this profile and a Good-ground mark of 1W4P in 15 runs makes the reserve jockey booking the only real worry.|

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Hanna
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up performer (headgear h) returning after 98 days; only one run of 6 on Good ground has produced a placing and the form string (7,5,F,6,9) leaves little encouragement even if Darren Collins has targeted this.|

races.paceDynamic: Run For The Border is the one confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him from the outset, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled gallop over 2m6f on Good ground at Ballinrobe. With a single pace-setter setting a measured tempo rather than a pressured one, the race will be run at a rhythm that suits travellers who can settle just off the pace — horses like It's Time Again, Ranger Billy, Whatyouwant and My Good Pal are ideally placed to track him without expending unnecessary energy early. The lack of pressure on the leader means the race is unlikely to develop into a true stamina test, instead rewarding horses who can quicken off a steady gallop in the straight, giving a clear advantage to prominent and near-prominent runners with a turn of foot. Several runners tagged as redistributed — including Light Her Up, Not So Serious, Tantrum Boy, Will It Be You and Coole Vision — are genuine hold-up types who will struggle to get their natural rear position in a field this size, meaning the race shape decisively favours those who can travel handily just behind the leader rather than closers relying on a truly-run test to bring them into contention.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Run For The Border dictates a comfortable gallop unchallenged and the winner comes from just off his heels
scenarios.body: Run For The Border sets a relaxed fractions, allowing the handy brigade to travel sweetly into contention turning for home; horses like Whatyouwant, It's Time Again and My Good Pal, able to settle close to the pace, are ideally placed to challenge when the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Run For The Border is allowed to pop every hurdle cleanly and the field never truly closes the gap in the straight
scenarios.body: With no rival to pressure him, Run For The Border can conserve enough energy to keep finding all the way to the line over this stamina-testing 2m6f; his recent form shows he is capable of front-running success and Good ground suits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Stays Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that true closers get into the race from off the bridle in the final turn
scenarios.body: Tannery Park, Bearami Creek or Ballinaboola Hanna, who possess genuine hold-up profiles and are not redistributed, would need the race to develop more of a test than the lone pace-setter is likely to provide; it is possible but depends on Run For The Border going hard early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes congestion, interference or a bunching incident in the early stages that scrambles the anticipated race shape
scenarios.body: With 19 runners over hurdles, fallers, impeded horses or a reshuffled order are a genuine possibility; in that scenario fresh legs from a horse who has been covered up like Coppola or My Good Pal could prove decisive in a ragged finish.

watchPoints.text: Run For The Border — if he misses or stumbles at an early hurdle, the controlled gallop immediately collapses and the entire race shape unravels, with no horse capable of immediately filling the lead.|

Whatyouwant and It's Time Again — both prominent types with headgear, they will be competing for the same tracking position just off Run For The Border; if they interfere with each other early in a 19-runner field, both chances are compromised.|

Coppola — his consistent placed efforts at this trip suggest he will be involved late, but his fade flag means the moment the leader quickens he may not find enough; watch whether Joshua Halford sends him prominent early to counteract this tendency.|

Light Her Up, Coole Vision and Will It Be You — three redistributed hold-up horses with reserve or unfancied jockeys who could create traffic problems in the middle of the field at the first few hurdles, which is a genuine risk in a 19-runner handicap hurdle.|

My Good Pal — the reserve jockey booking for a Gavin Cromwell horse with a strong prominent profile at this trip is worth monitoring at the declaration stage; if a named rider replaces the reserve, his profile becomes significantly more compelling.|

races.name: Sweeney Oil Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Pourquoi Poi
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner, clearly going to try to lead from the front again over a trip that suits on Good — style fit note flags it is racing in a prominent rather than lead role but in practice it is likely to hit the front; nine days since last run is fresh enough, and Paul Flynn's 3/21 strike rate in the two-week window is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Smackwater Jack
runners_data.note: Veteran 12-year-old who has won over 24f on Good, trainer Foster 1/2 in 14-day window; prominent style suits this shape and the class drop to OR 96 looks workable, though age and a 36-day absence are mild concerns.

runners_data.name: Fool Me Once
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Gavin Cromwell who has been off 74 days; Good-ground record is modest (0W3P from nine similar runs) and the moderate pace this race will likely generate may not be fast enough to set up his late challenge.

runners_data.name: Joshua Chamberlain
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 21f on Soft; has not won on Good in recent starts but the OR 95 mark and 69-day break for Gerard Keane's yard (0/6 in 14 days) tempers enthusiasm — needs to confirm he retains his form.

runners_data.name: Rushford
runners_data.note: True hold-up type but all recent form is over sprint trips of 8-12f, making this 2m6f assignment a significant stamina question; amateur rider Harry Sexton claims 7lb and the ⚠ fade flag adds further doubt at this distance.

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who showed a placed run over 22f on Good; Phillip Enright is a capable conditional and the 19-day turnaround for Brian McMahon is fine, though she has yet to win in recent outings and needs a strong pace to deliver her finish.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Serenade
runners_data.note: Ran second over 20f on Good most recently, making her the best-credentialled closer in the field on similar going; Eoghan Finegan claims 5lb, the 17-day break is straightforward, and if any hold-up horse can find a run in this field it is her.

runners_data.name: Yolanda's Star
runners_data.note: Limited form sample of just three runs, placed once over 16f on Good; unknown style makes her hard to place tactically, and the ⚠ fade flag and apprentice rider Joshua Halford combine to make her a speculative proposition over 2m6f.

runners_data.name: Stumblin In
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has placed multiple times on Good over similar trips; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim is useful but the 14/15 sim-going average finishing position suggests this horse finds it hard to get competitive in similar company.

runners_data.name: Strong Contender
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by nature, pushed into midfield on the map because the rear of the field is overcrowded — its true style is to sit and come late, which is less effective in a steady-pace scenario; J J Slevin adds class but OR 81 and a 36-day break limit expectations.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: Consistent four-year-old with three placings on Good, trained by Adrian McGuinness who is 2/28 in the 14-day window; prominent style suits the likely shape and the 11-day quick turnaround for a young horse bears watching, but the form profile gives him a legitimate place chance.

runners_data.name: Jolly Potter
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse who ends up mapped to midfield due to the surplus of wait-and-pounce types in this field; sparse hurdles form (only three runs), ⚠ fade flag and 67-day absence for James Fahey's yard combine to make this a very difficult conveyance to trust.

runners_data.name: Mollys Dolly
runners_data.note: Sits-and-waits by inclination but shifted towards midfield by the crowded hold-up contingent; OR 74 and a form string of PP-560 show no recent competitive effort, and even with Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim the profile is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: La Tene
runners_data.note: Another true hold-up type displaced toward midfield on the shape map; an 11-year-old with several pulled-up runs in recent form (P39F-P) and 61 days off, trained by John Patrick Ryan who is 5/25 in the 14-day window — hard to see a route to victory here.

runners_data.name: Lady Aquarelle
runners_data.note: Natural rear-of-field operator repositioned to midfield by the hold-up traffic; ⚠ fade flag, OR 72 and a sequence of poor finishes make her difficult to recommend, though Good ground is her best surface of those tried.

runners_data.name: Toor Moon
runners_data.note: Prominent type with four placed runs from 15 similar-going starts, suggesting honest consistency rather than winning ability; nine-year-old off 38 days for Ms M Flynn, and the form of 37-00U suggests a recent drop in form needs to be explained.

runners_data.name: Leis Fein
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 242 days off — a major flag in a big-field handicap hurdle; best form has come on softer ground and the 11-year-old's record in Good conditions (5/13 average) does not inspire confidence after such a long layoff.

runners_data.name: John Storey
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose last six starts include four pull-ups and a P; no jockey listed is another concern, and 100 days off for Ian Patrick Donoghue's yard (0/9 in 14 days) makes this a very hard watch — headgear (tp) has not unlocked improvement.

runners_data.name: Ladiam
runners_data.note: Well-suited prominent type who is consistent on Good ground (1W6P from 15 similar runs) and has been placed over almost identical trips repeatedly; OR 92 is near the top of this field, Norman Lee's yard (0/6 in 14 days) is quiet but Ladiam's profile makes it the most reliable prominent challenger to Pourquoi Poi.

races.paceDynamic: Pourquoi Poi is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m6f on Good ground — a shape that will not be pressured into overdoing it early. Ladiam, Smackwater Jack, Joshua Chamberlain, Granlahan and Toor Moon will look to press or track prominently, creating a compact group just off the pace rather than a strung-out procession. The field is loaded with nominal hold-up horses — Strong Contender, Jolly Potter, Mollys Dolly, La Tene and Lady Aquarelle are all true sit-and-wait types but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply not enough room at the rear for all of them in a field this size; of those, Strong Contender and Jolly Potter are most likely to secure a genuine hold-up berth. With one uncontested pace-setter dictating a steady tempo over a stamina-testing trip, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the gallop and sprint from the front of the chase group, rather than hold-up horses who will need an explosive late injection that an honest but moderate pace may not generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pourquoi Poi Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Pourquoi Poi crosses cleanly and is allowed to bowl along solo at a measured clip with no rival willing to close him down early.
scenarios.body: The lone front-runner sets an even tempo over the staying trip, leaving the prominent group just behind with energy banked; as the field approaches the business end, those tracking just off the pace are best placed to pounce on a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Packers Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster — Ladiam, Smackwater Jack and Joshua Chamberlain — push the gallop into a genuine staying test that grinds down Pourquoi Poi.
scenarios.body: A true stamina test develops as multiple prominent types refuse to let Pourquoi Poi dictate alone, raising the tempo and stretching the field; horses with proven staying form on Good ground in this prominent group then outlast the field up the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run and a true hold-up type can find clear passage through a big field.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners and several prominent types pressing, a genuine closer who secures a clear run could benefit from a truly run race; Whiskey Serenade or She'll Be Kept, both authentic hold-up types with good Going form, are the likeliest to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Big Field
scenarios.trigger: If early crowding, traffic and jumping errors in a 19-runner hurdle cause disruption that scrambles the anticipated race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Falls, unseats or significant interference reshuffle positions and open the race to a horse who finds a clear passage regardless of planned tactics; lightly exposed younger types or those with clean jumping records stand to benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Pourquoi Poi faces zero competition for the lead in a 19-runner field — if connections allow it to dictate an uncontested tempo over 2m6f on Good ground, the race may effectively be set up for the prominent pack rather than closers; watch how much Pourquoi Poi is asked to extend in the home straight.

With 19 runners over hurdles on Good ground, jumping errors and first-fence interference are a real risk — Strong Contender, Jolly Potter and Mollys Dolly are all hold-up types likely to be buried in midfield against their natural style and could be badly impeded if the field concertinas at early flights.

Leis Fein returns from a 242-day absence and Jolly Potter is 67 days off — both hold-up types with fitness questions; if either is asked to do more than their fitness allows, they could become obstacles rather than participants in a big competitive field.

Whiskey Serenade is the hold-up horse with the most credible recent form on similar going (2nd over 20f Good last time); if the pace quickens sufficiently in the final mile, she is the one to watch coming from off the pace as Eoghan Finegan's 5lb claim preserves her handicap weight advantage.

Granlahan and Ladiam represent the prominent-style horses with the most consistent placed form in similar conditions — if Pourquoi Poi weakens in the final 2f, watch whether it is a tracker from immediately behind or one slightly further back who first gets to the leader.
